head: cb201b4e1d348c90777bdde0b42b94c3538f19a5
summary:
I read every changed src and test file in cb201b4 and re-ran the checks myself. The full default suite passed (389/389), as did SL-063-DoneRowFinality (10/10) and the window cases C-008, C-001 and B-007 on the republished exe. Fitness passes all 62 rules. All seven findings are fixed the way the design asked, and the builder declared every departure I found.

- **HF-002:** TopLevelTracker.cs:101 sets OwnListedPartway using the same test as FolderTreeNode.Note (ChildCount > 0). Scanner.FolderDone commits the listing at line 279, before FolderExited runs at line 301, so the child count is already there when it is read. TopLevelRowText then says "could not be read in full", and both captions share one helper.
- **HF-004:** `_result` is gone.
- **HF-007 and HF-020:** For a Completed result, StartScan (MainWindow.xaml.cs:280) passes null, so ClearTopLevel runs and ShowFolderTree re-shows the panel. The Completed header branch is removed.
- **HF-012:** FigureText is now the only size and count formatter in src. The row-text classes are linked into Core.Tests.
- **HF-018:** DeleteFirst clears the read-only attribute before deleting. C-008 passes: a read-only stale report gives exit 2 with the path left empty, and a report held open gives exit 3 with the file left in place.
- **HF-019:** WorkAreaFit is fed the work area of the window's own monitor (MonitorFromWindow plus GetMonitorInfo, converted to DIPs). The MONITORINFO layout is 40 bytes and correct. The app has no DPI manifest, so it runs system-aware and the conversion is consistent.

One minor gap is filed. Nothing tests that HF-007/HF-020 changed anything, and the builder's own evidence for it does not show that it did: "topLevel absent" held before the fix too.

Second round: Round two found nothing new; my round-one finding m1 still stands. I went back over the changed code trying to break it. The diff adds no parser, matcher or reader, so the probing was of boundaries and failure paths.

- **HF-002 (partial listing):** The flag is right for every shape I tried:
  - a folder that could not be opened at all;
  - one whose first buffer failed after it opened (0 children, worded as the folder tree words it);
  - one that failed partway;
  - one that failed partway with subfolders still pending (Reading until done, then Unreadable with the flag);
  - one that failed partway in a stopped scan (StoppedPartway, no flag).
  
  The `_store!` in TopLevelTracker is safe because FolderExited only ever comes after Seed.
- **HF-018 (report delete-first):** An ACL refusal to clear read-only is caught and exits 3, as before. A hidden or system file deletes normally. A `.tmp` that is actually a folder exits 3, as it did before this slice.
- **HF-007/HF-020 (completed ending):** A rejected root, a failed scan and a root that could not be read all still clear the list. ShowOutcome returns early only for RootUnreadable, so a Completed scan always reaches ShowFolderTree. After a completed scan, a timer tick cannot refresh the list: Stop cancels the queued tick and `_progress` is set to null.
- **SL-063 test and the tick race:** Its TheResultsListShowsTheMarkOnATickAndAtTheEnding does feed RefreshTopLevel a Completed snapshot. So the builder's reason for leaving the tick race alone holds.
- **Test isolation:** `SynchronousIoCancel.Created` is `[ThreadStatic]` and the scan runs on the test thread, so TopLevelRowTextTests is safe to run in parallel.
- **HF-019 (monitor work area):** There is no DPI manifest, so the app is system-aware. GetMonitorInfo and TransformFromDevice therefore use the same coordinate space. A work area shorter than MinHeight behaves exactly as before.

**Already run in round one:** the full suite (389/389), the SL-063 bug tests (10/10), and window cases C-008, C-001 and B-007.

findings.claim: No test would notice if the HF-007/HF-020 change were undone. If StartScan went back to `ShowFinalTopLevel(failure is null ? result?.TopLevel : null)`, every test would still pass, and the completed scan's final rows would again be sorted and bound only to be thrown away. The builder cites C-001 and the C:\ProgramData run: 'topLevel absent and TopLevelList not in view, so the final list was not bound'. That conclusion does not follow. Both facts held before the fix: ShowFolderTree sets TopLevelList.ItemsSource and _shownTopLevel to null, and WindowReport writes topLevel only when both are non-null. HF-007's own evidence (WindowReport.cs:67-69) says exactly this. So the check is green whether or not the fix is there.
findings.evidence: src/FsAnalyser.App/MainWindow.xaml.cs:280 (the new Completed filter); MainWindow.xaml.cs:412-414 (ShowFolderTree clears ItemsSource and _shownTopLevel whichever way StartScan went); src/FsAnalyser.App/WindowReport.cs:215 (topLevel is written only when ShownTopLevel and ItemsSource are both set); tests/window/WindowCases.ps1 C-001 passes on both versions of the code. StartupHook.cs:854 already watches TopLevelList.ItemsSource changes, but only in its list modes.
findings.fix: Have the hook count the non-null TopLevelList.ItemsSource assignments made after ScanningPanel collapses; the ValueChanged listener in StartupHook.cs:854 already sees them. Report that count, and have C-001 assert it is 0 for a Completed ending, and 1 for the stopped-ending cases where the final list must still be bound.

obligations.evidence: src/FsAnalyser.Core/TopLevelTracker.cs:101 sets OwnListedPartway = unreadable && ChildCount(folder) > 0. The listing is already committed by Scanner.cs:279, before FolderExited at :301. TopLevelTracker.cs:202 publishes it only on Unreadable rows. src/FsAnalyser.App/TopLevelRowText.cs:27 words such a row '(could not be read in full)', and :40 words the count inside as 'could not be read (in full)'. MainWindow.xaml.cs:580-581 is the shared caption. tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/TopLevelRowTextTests.cs does a real scan with a 995 injected at b-big's third buffer. It asserts the errors [5,995,995,5] and files 1-1999, and checks both titles and the count wording. It passed in my run of the 389-test suite.

src/FsAnalyser.App/App.xaml.cs:122-128: DeleteFirst clears IsReadOnly, then deletes, for both the report and its .tmp. The WindowReport.cs doc names the one case left: a file held open without sharing delete. I ran tests/window/WindowCases.ps1 -Case C-008 on the republished exe. Read-only report and .tmp: exit 2, both gone. Held open: exit 3, still there. PASSED.

src/FsAnalyser.App/MainWindow.xaml.cs:125-140: OnSourceInitialized passes MonitorWorkArea() to WorkAreaFit.Fit. MonitorWorkArea gets the window monitor's rcWork from src/FsAnalyser.Core/Native/Monitors.cs, converts it with TransformFromDevice, and falls back to SystemParameters.WorkArea only when the query fails. The constructor's height clamp against the primary is removed. src/FsAnalyser.App/WorkAreaFit.cs is the pure rule. WorkAreaFitTests.AWindowPlacedOnAMonitorBelowThePrimaryStaysOnIt gives it a 1080-2112 work area below the primary and the window keeps Top 1106. B-007 passed in my run on the one monitor here. Never run on a real second monitor or with mixed DPI; the builder already listed this as left open.

cases.evidence: HF-002. tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/TopLevelRowTextTests.cs builds a real temp tree. b-big and c-top\big each hold 2,000 files with 100-character names, so their listings take several buffers. OverrideQueryError returns 995 at the third buffer of just those two folders, and a-denied and c-top\denied are denied FILE_LIST_DIRECTORY. The test asserts the partial-listing shape itself (Unreadable, ListedPartway true, Files in 1..1999), the never-opened shape (Files 0, ListedPartway false), and the exact words for both plus the count inside c-top. The builder saw it fail on the title before the fix.

HF-018. tests/window/WindowCases.ps1 Test-C008 writes a stale report and .tmp and sets both ReadOnly. It runs the published exe with --report and no root, then asserts exit 2 and that both files are gone. It also holds the report open with FileShare.Read and asserts exit 3 and that the file stays. I ran it: PASSED.

HF-019. WorkAreaFitTests passes WorkAreaFit.Fit a work area below the primary (1080-2112, window at 1106), a monitor taller than the primary, a foot below the work area, and a window taller than the work area. The monitor-below-the-primary input reaches the rule that decides placement. It does not reach MainWindow.MonitorWorkArea on a non-primary monitor, because this PC has one monitor, so going back to SystemParameters.WorkArea there would pass. That limit is recorded as left open, and nothing on this machine can test it.

drift: No undeclared departures. The builder declared all six I found: FigureText instead of SizeText; TopLevelRowText split into a partial class with an init-only ListedPartway; the kinds caption reworded to 'may be missing'; the WindowReport exit contract narrowed for a report held open without sharing delete; Monitors placed in Core/Native with the height clamp moved to OnSourceInitialized; and the tick race that can show a Completed final snapshot under the 'before the stop' header. I checked that race against the dispatcher priorities. The ending's continuation runs at Normal, ahead of Render, so the wrong header is replaced before it is drawn.
No undeclared departures. The builder declared all six, and round two found no others.
